subject: MAP: Lead-time Hedging & Trial-to-Commit Cadence for Dedicated/Private Pools
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@heliumhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP ask: lead times, trial-to-commit cadence for Private/Dedicated pools

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering asked me to capture a short list of asks so we can build a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) around capacity reservation for a Private deployment. High level items we need addressed for our internal approval:

- Typical lead times (order to capacity on customer VPC) for Dedicated vs Private (on-prem/VPC) tranches, and hedging options for long lead items (GPUs, network).
- Recommended trial-to-commit cadence: how many weeks of evaluation do you recommend before we lock capacity commitments, and what are the guardrails for rolling down/up?
- GPU pool sizing guidance: starter tranche for our projected 5k qps embedding workload (rough split by model family, memory/VRAM profiles).
- Procurement asks: contract cadence, cancellation windows, credits for early termination or capacity underuse (high level).

We have a narrow window — execs want a show of runway and a draft MAP by next Wednesday so procurement + legal can review. Attaching an internal helix of what we think is sensible as a starting point. Would appreciate Redwood's guidance and a proposed mutual timeline.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Infrastructure, Helium Health
[Attachment: Helium MAP draft v1.pdf]
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask: lead times, trial-to-commit cadence for Private/Dedicated pools

Olivia —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick read-through below and a proposed next step. I copied Laura and Ben to pull in sizing/ops detail and procurement language.

High level response (summary):
- Lead times: Dedicated (hosted reserved pools) typically 4–6 weeks to guarantee tranche throughput; Private/VPC deployments are 6–10 weeks depending on region and customer network setup. We can offer a staged ramp for Private: initial staging nodes in 2–3 weeks (limited capacity), then full tranche by week 6–10.
- Trial cadence: typical eval window is 2–4 weeks for smoke + performance, followed by a 4–8 week pilot for production-like load. For customers who want faster lock-in, we offer a 30-day pilot with pro-rated credits toward a 6‑month reservation.
- Sizing: rough starter guidance below; Laura will add specifics.
- Procurement: we can be flexible on termination credits for the first tranche if the customer commits to a 6‑12 month term; Ben will outline standard contract levers.

Proposed next step: 45-minute MAP workshop early next week to align timelines and acceptance criteria. I attached our reserve-playbook template to use as the shared MMP (mutual milestone plan).

Best,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserve-playbook-template.xlsx]

Olivia / team —

Thanks — I pulled together a concise runway + contingency plan you can drop into the MAP template Rafael sent. Key recommendations below (aimed at minimizing risk while keeping unit cost predictable):

1) Recommended starter tranche (based on your 5k qps embedding estimate):
   - Phase 1 (pilot): 4 x A100-80GB equiv nodes (optimized for embeddings, KV cache enabled) — supports baseline latency SLA for developer testing and small-scale UAT (2–4 weeks).
   - Phase 2 (pilot+production): add 8 x A100-80GB equiv nodes (total 12) for steady-state throughput and redundancy — targets 95th percentile latency SLO under 70ms for single-shard requests.
   - Buffer tranche: +20% (3 nodes) reserved as surge capacity for peak testing and rollout.

2) Lead time and hedging:
   - Dedicated hosted pools: reserve confirmation to capacity in ~4 weeks; we hedge supplier lead risk by offering short-term burstable capacity on our shared pools for weeks 1–4 while hardware arrives.
   - Private/VPC: typical 6–9 weeks depending on firewall/VPN provisioning. We recommend a two-step acceptance: staging baseline (at reduced capacity) within 2–3 weeks, and full handover by week 6–9.

3) Trial-to-commit cadence and commercial levers:
   - Option A (fast path): 30-day pilot, pro-rated credits applied to a 6‑month committed tranche. Early-termination credit = 50% of unused committed months for first tranche only.
   - Option B (gradual path): 8-week pilot, followed by a 6–12 month commitment with standard termination notice (60 days) and a smaller early-termination credit.

4) Acceptance criteria (to put in MAP):
   - Performance: p95 latency < 80ms on benchmark prompt set; throughput within 10% of target requests/sec; no more than 2 production SEVs in 14 days post-handover.
   - Security/compliance: SOC2 readiness checklist completed and evidence uploaded before full tranche activation.

Next steps I recommend we capture in the MAP workshop: milestones, owners (Redwood infra lead + Helium infra lead), procurement signoff date, and DocuSign target. I dropped a short SOC2 checklist as an attachment for procurement/legal to review.

Laura Bennett
Director, Solution Architecture, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf]
